scope: Every Characters row with more than one explicitly recorded reading; no missing readings are added.
policy: Editorial review requested by the project owner. Exact imported rows and existing reviewed meanings remain intact. Separate meanings only where cited dictionaries support the exact readings; identical meanings remain grouped. Explicit source-reviewed pronunciation choices are applied only to unchanged original tuples and disclose their original readings and source disagreement. Historical and regional context remains independent of etymology and geometry.

伲.note: This card uses dictionary-attested nì / nǐ as an explicit editorial pronunciation choice. The original Unihan ní / nǐ remains preserved: Unicode’s 2023 proposal records a change from nì to ní, whereas CC-CEDICT and Han Dian attach the dialectal I/we/my/our senses to nì. Taiwan MOE identifies nǐ as an old variant meaning you. This is a documented source disagreement, not a claim that Unihan has a typo. Audio uses Mandarin syllables, not a recording of Shanghai dialect speech.
伲.zdic: The exact entry explicitly distinguishes nì dialectal I/we/my/our from nǐ, the historical variant of you.

readingRevision.source: Owner-requested lexical reading reconciliation: CC-CEDICT and Han Dian nì dialect pronoun; Taiwan MOE nǐ historical variant of you. Original Unihan ní is retained and its differing 2023 revision is disclosed.
